title: The Flaw of Selecting People Before Deciding on Strategy
author: Admired Leadership
summary: The post warns leaders reorganizing in response to market change against placing people on the org chart before settling strategy. The temptation comes from wanting to reward loyal team members, but it lets strategy be shaped by who can do what instead of what is best for the enterprise. The author prescribes a fixed sequence of strategy, then structure, then people. Structure covers the number of teams, leadership roles and processes needed to execute the plan. Only then should people be matched to roles, which may mean a favored member lacks a seat or new talent is needed.
points: Seating people before choosing strategy is called a colossal mistake that puts the cart before the horse.
The temptation arises from a desire to reward loyal team members who paved the way.
The prescribed order for any reorganization is strategy, then structure, then people.
Following the sequence permits objective decisions even when it leaves a favored colleague without a role.
quotes: As leaders draw a new map for the future, they are naturally concerned with how to reward loyal team members who have paved the way.
The best leaders resist the urge to place people on the org chart before they know the strategy.
A leader who puts people into positions without a clear connection to a larger strategy is putting the cart in front of the horse.
In that scenario, strategy emerges as a result of who can do what rather than what is best for the enterprise.
Structures might include the number of teams needed and which leadership roles are required, not to mention the design of processes needed to allow efficient execution of the strategy.
Sometimes, this means a favored team member may not have a seat or that new talent will be needed to execute and achieve the desired outcomes.
